<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Air pollution is a significant environmental issue with widespread impacts on public health. Evidence on the causal effect of air pollution control policies on weight‐related outcomes remains limited. This study fills this gap by leveraging the Air Pollution Prevention and Control Action Plan as a quasi‐natural experiment, combining four waves (2010, 2012, 2014, 2016) of panel data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS). Employing a difference‐in‐differences framework, we find that implementing this policy significantly reduces overweight risk among residents. Mechanism analyses indicate that the policy primarily lowers overweight risk by increasing physical exercise frequency and alleviating depressive symptoms. Further heterogeneity analyses show this impact is particularly pronounced among urban residents, young adults, females, and individuals with lower educational attainment. Our findings clarify the causal link between environmental regulation and population health, and provide actionable insights for policymakers to design coordinated interventions that leverage air quality improvements to advance public health goals.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper explores the role of Standard Essential Patents (SEPs) in shaping technological development and regional innovation in Europe’s telecommunications sector. Results reveal strong geographic concentration: Helsinki and Stockholm account for one-third of all cellular SEPs. Unlike other technologies, SEP distribution does not scale with population or prior technological expertise. Findings suggest a “rich-get-richer” dynamic where early leadership reinforces future dominance; however, this advantage weakens across technological generations. This study offers new insights into standardization’s spatial dynamics and underscores the need for long-term perspectives when modeling technological competition and diffusion.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As the Journal of Economic Geography turns 25, this commentary reflects on the field’s representations of care and directions for future research. In much of economic geography, care remains an absence, deemed peripheral to the economy. Yet for decades, scholars have shown that care exerts a pervasive influence as a foundation of economic activity. Care is also an increasingly important frontier for firms, finance and technology. Finally, care acts as a catalyst for rethinking and reorganising economic geographies. Reviewing existing work, I outline research agendas to address the distorting marginalisation of care and its transformative potential.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This systematic review critically examines empirical research on retirement financial planning (RFP) in China, framed by the PRISMA guidelines and the “C‐RFP‐C” protocol. The protocol is registered at OSF (
                    <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="https://osf.io/f3nps">https://osf.io/f3nps</jats:ext-link>
                    ). Specialized databases such as EconLit, Business Source Premier, ABI/INFORM, Social Sciences Citation Index, and AgeLine were used, as well as multidisciplinary databases and Chinese‐language sources (CNKI and Wanfang). The search strategies employed yielded a total of 2035 documents related to RFP within the Chinese context. After rigorous screening and quality appraisal, 55 studies met the established inclusion criteria and were synthesized qualitatively. The synthesis highlights the central role of financial literacy in RFP, alongside the influence of psychological, social, and institutional factors. Across studies, persistent disparities emerge across gender and between urban and rural populations. Motivational factors such as future orientation and goal clarity shape willingness to plan and save, while opportunities for retirement planning are strongly conditioned by income, asset ownership, pension design, and access to financial and digital infrastructure. Overall, the findings underscore the multidimensional and context‐dependent nature of RFP in China, as structured by the interaction of capacity, willingness, and opportunity.
                  </jats:p>

                  <jats:p>Cointegrating rank selection is studied in a function space reduced rank regression where the data are time series of cross‐section curves. Consistent cointegrating rank estimation is developed using information criteria extended to curve time series environments. The asymptotic theory involves two‐parameter Gaussian processes that generalise the standard limit processes involved in cointegrating regressions. Simulations provide evidence of the effectiveness of consistent rank selection by the BIC criterion and the tendency of AIC to overestimate order as in standard lag order selection in autoregression, as well as in reduced rank regression with multiple time series.</jats:p>

                  <jats:p>A central assumption for identifying structural shocks in vector autoregressive (VAR) models via heteroskedasticity is the time‐invariance of the impact effects of the shocks. It is shown how that assumption can be tested when long‐run restrictions based on the cointegration structure of the variables are available for identifying structural shocks. The importance of performing such tests is illustrated by investigating the impact of fundamental shocks on stock prices in the U.S. It is found that fundamental shocks post‐1986 have become more important than in the pre‐1986 period.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper examines the unintended consequences of the 2018–2019 US‐China trade war for Vietnam, a key bystander economy, using quarterly HS 8‐digit US import data from 2017Q1 to 2020Q4. While the average treatment effect on Vietnam's exports to the US is small and statistically insignificant, substantial heterogeneity arises from pre‐war revealed comparative advantages (RCAs). Vietnam experienced markedly stronger export growth in sectors where China held high pre‐war RCA, consistent with trade diversion and substitution effects. These gains were nonlinear and most pronounced in sectors where Vietnam initially had low comparative advantage, reflecting the exploitation of previously untapped export opportunities. Consequently, Vietnam captured meaningful trade‐diversion benefits primarily outside its pre‐existing areas of comparative strength. In addition, we provide consistent evidence that the relocation of MNCs is strongly associated with the observed export surge. By quantifying these spillovers, our study contributes to the literature on global value chain dynamics and trade protectionism.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper investigates whether and how U.S. exporters circumvent China's anti‐dumping (AD) measures by re‐routing trade through third countries. Using detailed data on AD cases and monthly trade flows of China and U.S. from 2002 to 2011, we apply a triple‐differences (DDD) approach to identify abnormal trade‐flow adjustments consistent with third‐country re‐routing. We find evidence of such patterns in a subset of cases following final AD rulings. Product characteristics, such as lower differentiation, higher financial leverage, and greater inventory pressure, are associated with variation in the feasibility and intensity of circumvention. Moreover, circumvention tends to occur through countries that are institutionally closer to the U.S. and geographically concentrated in Asia‐Oceania routes. The possible circumvention emerges after final rulings rather than during investigations.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Oil is the lifeblood of industry, serving as the core source of power for the operation of industrial machinery. Ensuring its stable supply is crucial for the smooth production process, which in turn is a key determinant in enhancing the quality of export products for enterprises. This study empirically examines the impact of energy supply on the quality of export products and the mechanism of its effect by using a staggered difference‐in‐differences (DID) method with the implementation of China's West‐to‐East Oil Transportation Project as a quasi‐natural experiment. The empirical results show that a dependable energy supply substantially boosts the quality of goods produced for export by various companies. The mechanism analysis shows that energy supply improves export product quality through enterprise performance improvement effects, industry agglomeration effects and supply chain stabilization effects, and it mainly improves export product quality in energy‐importing regions, technology‐intensive industries, private enterprises, and general trade enterprises. Further analysis reveals that a stable supply of energy helps enhance the sustainability of enterprise exports while helping enterprises realize value chain upgrading, helping China get rid of the curse of locking the bottom of the export value chain. The findings of this study help clarify the intrinsic mechanism between energy supply and export product quality and provide an empirical basis for the cross‐regional energy dispatch strategy to help China's export value chain upgrade.</jats:p>
